subject: Mathematics

source.topic: Numbers, operations and relationships: Place value (numbers between 11 and 25)
source.subtopic: Decompose two-digit numbers into multiples of tens and units/ones to 15 (weeks 1-4), 20 (weeks 5-6) and 25 (weeks 7-10)

show.line: Fourteen is one ten and four ones. One bundle of ten sticks, and four loose sticks. Ten and four, fourteen!

rounds.prompt: One bundle of ten and three loose sticks. How many sticks? Tap the number.
Which picture shows one ten and five ones?
rounds.praise: Yes! One ten and five ones is fifteen.

rounds.prompt: Twelve. How many ones are with the ten? Say the number.
Two tens and one one. Which number is it?
Two bundles of ten and four loose sticks. How many sticks?
In the number eighteen, which digit tells us about the tens?
rounds.praise: Yes! The one means one ten. The eight means eight ones.

hints: A bundle is ten. Count the bundles first, then the loose ones.
The first digit says how many tens. The second says how many ones.

beat_the_tutor.setup: My turn! I will break up the number fifteen.
beat_the_tutor.tutor_try: Fifteen is five tens and one one!
beat_the_tutor.win_line: You caught me! Fifteen is one ten and five ones. Ten and five.
beat_the_tutor.gentle_line: Let's look together. One bundle of ten, five loose. Fifteen!

parent_line: Can break a number up to 25 into tens and ones.
